---
title: "Use the viewer"
guide-section: How-to guides
---

Press `?` in the viewer for every key and mouse action.

## Move around

The wheel zooms (with Shift time only, with Ctrl distance only), and the arrows pan. In the pan tool a drag moves the view; in any tool the middle button, or Space and drag, does. Tab moves on by a screen in time, and Shift+Tab back. The strip under the time axis is the whole recording: click or drag on it to move the window, and press `b` to go back to the view before a jump. `w` fits the whole recording.

## Set the colours

Drag the top or bottom of the colour bar to move that limit, or its middle to move both. A click on it, or `a`, sets the limits from what is on screen. The Display panel picks the colour map, the statistic a pixel shows and a log scale.

## Annotate

1. Pick a tool: `1` point, `2` path, `3` polygon, `4` box.
2. Click to place points. End a path or polygon with Enter, a double-click or a right-click.
3. Type a label in the box that opens, or press Enter to keep the last one.

Drawings go into the set being edited and are saved as you go. To edit, switch to the select tool (`v`, or double-click): drag an annotation or a vertex to move it, double-click a side to add a vertex, and press Delete to remove.

## Correct someone else's annotations

Select them and press `c` to copy them into your own set. Each copy records where it came from in `derived_from` and `derived_revision`. Only a set's owner can change it.

## Move sets between the viewer and DASCore

"download" gives the set being edited as a zip of its folder. "load" makes a new set from such a zip, or from a table of annotations (`.parquet` or `.csv`).

## Download an area

1. In the Download panel, take an area: from the selected annotation, from the window on screen, or by dragging a box (`d`).
2. Tick the products to take; it shows their size.
3. Press download for one DASDAE file, or Sync (under `dastor browse --data-dir`) to write it into your local data directory.

A synced file is named for the recording, the product and the start of the area, with a number added if that name is taken, so nothing is replaced. The directory's spool sees it when it next indexes (`spool.update()`).

## Choose the levels to zoom through

The Levels panel lists a recording's [products](31-products.qmd) from coarse to fine. Tick the ones to zoom through. The control at the bottom right shows the level on screen; click it to hold the view on one level, and choose "auto" to follow the zoom again.
